An offline Markdown editor and reader for Windows, macOS and Linux. Write directly in the rendered document, browse local folders, and work with diagrams, equations, tables and images. Electron and Chromium are included; local editing needs no account, WebView2 or .NET.

[Download the latest release](https://github.com/lferraro1103/Lecat-Markdown/releases/latest) · [Release notes](https://github.com/lferraro1103/Lecat-Markdown/releases)

## Features

- **Three document modes:** visual editing, reading, and Markdown source with preview. Includes formatting, undo/redo and find/replace.
- **Two documents side by side:** drag tabs or use their context menu. Independent editing, history, mode and scrolling, an adjustable divider, and layout restoration for saved files.
- **Compact interface:** file details unfold from the tab; save status sits beside Search. Toggle the floating formatting toolbar and right-click to choose one of five positions.
- **Rich Markdown:** offline Mermaid diagrams, LaTeX math with KaTeX, highlighted code, task lists, tables and local images.
- **File navigation:** filter files and folders, use Windows folder history and quick access, or choose files with the native macOS dialog. Mac tabs integrate into the top toolbar.
- **File tools:** create files and folders, create Markdown from the clipboard, browse recent documents and inspect file metadata.
- **Export and printing:** PDF, HTML, EPUB and PNG; SVG for diagrams. Native printing includes font-size and scale options.
- **Native integration:** Quick Look previews on Mac and system sharing on Windows/macOS. Copy Markdown remains a separate action.
- **Workspace:** outline, focus mode, zoom, trackpad pinch, always-on-top windows, and light, dark or system themes.
- **Recovery:** restore open documents and the selected tab, recover unsaved drafts and detect external changes before overwriting files. Welcome appears only on first use.
- **Settings:** English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese; optional beta updates.
- **Commands and links:** install the `lecat` command from Settings and use `lecat://file/…` links. Custom application links require confirmation; saved permissions can be revoked.

Mac packages use ad-hoc integrity signatures; they are not Developer ID signed or notarized. See the macOS installation and signing guides in Documentation.

## Homebrew (macOS)

```sh
brew tap lferraro1103/lecat-markdown https://github.com/lferraro1103/Lecat-Markdown
brew install --cask lferraro1103/lecat-markdown/lecat-markdown
```

## Working with documents

Open a Markdown file or create a document. **Visual editing** is the default: click a heading, paragraph, list or table cell and type. Switch to **Reading** or **Code and preview** when needed. Diagrams and equations have focused editing dialogs; unchanged blocks retain their original Markdown.

To compare documents, drag one tab onto another and choose the left or right side, or use the tab's context menu. Click a pane to select it: search, formatting, saving, sharing and export follow that document. Resize the divider or return to a single pane without closing the other tabs. Layout restoration requires both files to have saved paths.

Saving is explicit: the original file changes only when you save. If another application modifies it, Lecat reports the conflict and lets you save a separate copy. To restore automatic theme selection, choose **View → Use system theme**.

## Updates

- **Installed Windows app and supported Mac editions:** use Help → Check for updates to find, download and install public releases. The Windows portable ZIP requires a manual update.
- **macOS 12:** stay on the separate Monterey release channel. Mac 3.2.5 or earlier needs one manual installation of a newer edition to enable the current updater.
- **Linux:** download and install the new AppImage or `.deb` manually. Beta releases are optional in Settings. Checking and downloading updates requires internet access.

## Keyboard shortcuts

Use `Ctrl` on Windows/Linux and `⌘` on macOS. Shortcuts act on the selected document pane.

| Action | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| New document / open file / open folder | `Ctrl+N / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+Shift+O` |
| Save / Save As | `Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S` |
| Close tab | `Ctrl+W` |
| Reading / visual editing / source and preview | `Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2 / Ctrl+3` |
| Find | `Ctrl+F` |
| Find and replace | `Ctrl+Alt+F` |
| Bold / italic | `Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I` |
| Toggle file explorer | `Ctrl+Shift+E` |
| Focus mode / change theme | `Ctrl+Shift+F / Ctrl+Shift+T` |
| Export PDF | `Ctrl+Alt+P` |
| Export options | `Ctrl+Alt+E` |
| Print | `Ctrl+P` |
| Zoom in / out / reset | `Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0` |
| Tab context menu | `Shift+F10` |

## Local data and formats

Preferences and recovery drafts stay on your computer. The historical profile folder name `ClaroMD` is retained for compatibility.

| System | Profile location |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%/ClaroMD` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/ClaroMD` |
| Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ClaroMD · ~/.config/ClaroMD` |

On Linux, `~/.config` is the fallback when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset. There is no cloud synchronization or telemetry.

Supports UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM and UTF-16 LE, preserving LF/CRLF line endings. The document limit is 20 MB. UTF-16 BE and invalid UTF-8 are rejected to prevent data corruption.

Remote images are not downloaded automatically. Web links open only when clicked; Markdown scripts do not execute. Mermaid errors are isolated to their blocks. PlantUML and Graphviz blocks are displayed as source code.

## Development

Requirements: Node.js **22.12 or later**, npm and a supported desktop platform.

```sh
npm ci
node scripts/prepare-electron.cjs
npm test
npm start
```

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Windows portable distribution | `npm run dist` |
| Windows installer | `npm run installer` |
| macOS Apple Silicon packages | `npm run dist:mac -- --arm64` |
| macOS Intel packages | `npm run dist:mac -- --x64` |
| Linux x64 AppImage and .deb | `npm run dist:linux` |
| Existing Electron integration audit | `npm run audit` |

The application entry point is `electron/`; `src/` contains the historical WinForms/WebView2 implementation. Dependencies are pinned in `package-lock.json`. Audit screenshots and results are generated in `docs/previews/electron` and excluded from Git because they can contain local paths. Regenerate all six READMEs with `node scripts/generate-readmes.cjs` after editing `docs/readme/*.json`; check consistency with `node scripts/generate-readmes.cjs --check`.
